Width adaptation remains unshipped.

The first two-child generated-top data-free slice is also shipped: isf/atl_two_child_pipeline.isf emits parent, reader, writer, and generated top .fsm artifacts for sequential reader.capture/reader.done then writer.emit/writer.done handoffs.

Downstream consumers should read the resolved child metadata from actor_network.instances[], trigger evidence from actor_network.transaction_triggers[], event evidence from actor_network.event_waits[], and the generated-top discovery plus per-child wiring metadata from actor_network.generated_tops[].children[].

The selected resolved-child trigger-batch generated-top slice is also shipped: isf/atl_two_child_trigger_batch_pipeline.isf emits parent, reader, writer, and generated top .fsm artifacts for one contiguous same-cycle trigger batch over reader.capture and writer.emit, followed by source-ordered waits on reader.done and writer.done.

Downstream producers may emit that exact form only when there are exactly two resolved children, no static group declaration, no ATL data movement in the transaction segment, and no repeated child activations or waits. Downstream consumers should read trigger evidence from actor_network.transaction_triggers[], wait evidence from actor_network.event_waits[], task-scoped temporary association evidence from actor_network.association_schedules[], schema-version-1 compatibility schedule evidence from actor_network.group_schedules[], and generated-top discovery from actor_network.generated_tops[] with kind resolved_children_trigger_batch_event_sequence.

The first generated-child actor-to-actor route through that generated top is shipped by isf/atl_two_child_data_pipeline.isf.

Downstream producers may emit one named drive body pair (writer.payload reader.payload) between two resolved children when the parent transaction is ordered as trigger reader.capture, await reader.done, drive forward_payload, trigger writer.emit, await writer.done, then complete.

The parent exposes reader_payload as the generated source handoff input and writer_payload as the generated sink handoff output; the generated top wires reader.payload to parent reader_payload and parent writer_payload to writer.payload.

Downstream consumers should read one-bit route provenance from actor_network.data_movements[] with kind: "scalar_actor_handoff" and generated-top discovery from actor_network.generated_tops[] with children[].

No new report family or public data_links key is exposed.

The exact-width vector generated-child actor-to-actor route is shipped by isf/atl_two_child_vector_data_pipeline.isf.

Downstream producers may emit the same (sink source) drive-body pair between two resolved children when the source endpoint is a child output, the sink endpoint is a child input, and both endpoint declarations have the same positive width. The parent source handoff, parent sink handoff, child interface roles, generated top links, and generated HDL links use that exact width. Schedule JSON keeps the same route entry shape and reports kind: "vector_actor_handoff", width equal to the endpoint width, and width_source: "resolved_child_endpoint_exact_width".

The bounded multi-route form is shipped by isf/atl_two_child_multi_data_pipeline.isf.

Downstream producers may emit multiple named actor-to-actor drive bodies in the same parent transaction only when all routes share the same resolved source child, the same resolved sink child, one direct endpoint pair per drive body, matching source/sink endpoint widths for each route, and one argument-free top-level drive call per route.

The accepted route segment is contiguous: source trigger, source event wait, all route drive calls, sink trigger, sink event wait. The shipped fixture moves payload and sideband from reader to writer through separate route drive calls and separate generated parent handoffs.

Downstream consumers still read every route from actor_network.data_movements[]: scalar one-bit routes use kind: "scalar_actor_handoff", and exact-width vector routes use kind: "vector_actor_handoff". Generated-top discovery still uses actor_network.generated_tops[] with children[]. No new report family or public data_links key is exposed.

Downstream producers must still treat broader actor-to-actor generated-child routes, fan-in/fan-out source or sink sets, width adaptation, route mux/storage, CDC/reset remapping, ready/backpressure, payload protocols, recursive actor networks, repeated triggers, trigger-batch plus data movement coupling, groups, cross-transaction continuation, and permanent actor grouping as deferred. A shipped route segment fails closed if its drive calls do not follow the source event wait and precede the sink trigger.

Downstream producers must also keep the route drive unparameterized and the route drive call argument-free. Parameterized route drive definitions and route drive calls with actual arguments remain fail-closed before drive actual binding, expression movement, or payload protocols are inferred. That same route-drive argument boundary applies to the shipped generated-top pin-ingress and pin-egress route families; route drive calls are one-cycle timing points, not parameterized payload-binding calls.

The route source must remain one scalar endpoint. A drive-body source expression such as (writer.payload (+ reader.payload 1)) remains fail-closed before FSMGen infers expression movement, payload transformation, storage, muxing, or backpressure behavior.

The shipped FSMGen hardening around this route keeps the downstream surface bounded.

It adds focused fail-closed coverage for adjacent invalid shapes: the source endpoint must be a scalar output on the source child, the sink endpoint must be a scalar input on the sink child, every selected route drive body must contain exactly one endpoint pair, and each route must be activated by exactly one top-level drive call.

Downstream producers should keep emitting only the shipped same-source, same-sink scalar or exact-width vector route set until a later spec update explicitly widens the contract.

The shipped width hardening now accepts same-width generated-child actor-to-actor routes. Wider source child outputs paired with one-bit sink inputs, one-bit source outputs paired with wider sink inputs, and any other source/sink width mismatch remain fail-closed. Downstream producers should not assume truncation, extension, packing, slicing, payload protocols, muxing, or storage insertion.

The shipped clock/reset hardening keeps the generated-child actor-to-actor route in one parent clock/reset policy.

Source or sink child clock/reset mismatches fail closed until FSMGen publishes an explicit CDC bridge or reset-remapping contract; downstream producers should not assume generated system-port remapping, async crossing logic, route storage, muxing, or backpressure insertion.

The shipped self-route hardening keeps the generated-child actor-to-actor route between two distinct resolved children.

Same-child source/sink route pairs fail closed; downstream producers should not assume self-route, loopback, child-internal bypass, storage, muxing, fan-in/fan-out, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped repeated-trigger hardening keeps the route sequence to one source-child trigger and one sink-child trigger.

Extra route-child triggers fail closed; downstream producers should not assume repeated activation, restart, pending-request merging, trigger fan-in/fan-out, or multi-activation scheduling until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped repeated-wait hardening keeps the same route sequence to one source-child event wait and one sink-child event wait.

Extra route-child waits fail closed; downstream producers should not assume event fan-in/fan-out, repeated wait sequencing, child replay, route-level wait storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped same-parent-transaction hardening keeps the entire route sequence inside one parent transaction.

Downstream producers must not split the source trigger, source wait, data drive call, sink trigger, and sink wait across multiple parent transactions or assume route continuation, pending handoff storage, transaction rendezvous, cross-transaction scheduling, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped sink-trigger ordering hardening keeps the route data drive call before the sink child trigger.

Downstream producers must not trigger the sink child before the drive call or assume speculative sink activation, delayed payload delivery, route storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped sink-event-wait ordering hardening keeps the sink child event wait after the sink child trigger.

Downstream producers must not wait on the sink child event before triggering that child or assume pre-trigger acknowledgement, sticky event sampling, event replay, route storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped source-event-wait ordering hardening keeps the source child event wait after the source child trigger.

Downstream producers must not wait on the source child event before triggering that child or assume pre-trigger acknowledgement, sticky event sampling, event replay, route storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped route-contiguity hardening keeps the same route as one contiguous transaction-body segment.

Downstream producers must not interleave unrelated parent transaction clauses between the source trigger, source event wait, data drive call, sink trigger, and sink event wait or assume interleaved parent work, local side effects, pre/post route sampling, route continuation, pending handoff storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped route-isolation hardening keeps that contiguous segment as the only executable parent transaction-body work between the transaction start condition and completion.

Downstream producers must not emit unrelated parent clauses before the source trigger or after the sink event wait, or assume pre-route setup, post-route sampling, local side effects, cleanup work, route continuation, pending handoff storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped route-boundary cardinality hardening keeps that isolated route bounded by exactly one simple (on ...) start condition and exactly one simple (complete ...) completion pulse.

Downstream producers must not emit extra start boundaries or extra completion boundaries around the route, or assume activation fan-in, completion fan-out, start-condition arbitration, local setup/cleanup, route continuation, pending handoff storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

The shipped boundary-simplicity hardening keeps those two route boundaries body-free.

Downstream producers must not emit (on ...) activation-body samples or (complete ...) extra payload operands around the route, or assume activation-body sampling, completion payload/fan-out, local setup/cleanup, route continuation, pending handoff storage, muxing, backpressure, or payload insertion until FSMGen publishes an explicit contract for those behaviors.

13. Scheduled .fsm Review Artifact

Downstream tools should treat the scheduled .fsm files as review artifacts and as the input to FSMGen’s HDL backend, not as a general stable AST API. Stable machine consumption should prefer the schedule JSON and manifest key families.

Important .fsm lowering conventions:

  • Every accepted transaction lowers to explicit state blocks.
  • Drives and rules lower to non-state DT blocks.
  • = is combinational.
  • <-, <=, and <1 are sequential/operator families in the public contract.
  • <1 is used for one-cycle delayed pulses such as completion and rule trigger sources.
  • Generated top files use canonical Lisp-ish ?wiring links.
  • Multi-domain accepted event-crossing actors emit domain .fsm artifacts, a generated top .fsm, and generated CDC child interface metadata.
  • Multiple accepted event crossings in one actor emit one generated CDC child interface and one report entry per crossing.

Deterministic DT ordering:

transaction and rule DT blocks keep construction order;
generated rule-trigger fan-in DT blocks follow rule DTs by transaction name;
hash-backed drive DT blocks are sorted lexically by drive name

14. Schedule JSON Report

Declared interface metadata is independent of inferred hardware. Successful check/semantic reports for directly parsed ISF sources include optional source.interface_ports; schedule reports include interface_ports, and each realized clock_domains entry includes its owned declarations with the same schema. Inputs precede outputs, preserving authored order within each direction. Unused/undriven declarations remain present; clock/reset pins and generated private handoffs do not enter this census. A known empty interface is []; unknown caller-provided declaration metadata is null in schedule reports. Unrelated formats and failure source reports omit this optional source field.

Entries require name, direction and positive width; optional type keeps the authored local/imported alias, type_kind its resolved kind, and domain the named owning domain. Scalar source aliases currently resolve to bit or bits; admitted packed record actor inputs/outputs resolve to record and carry ordered scalar-leaf fields: path, width, lsb, msb, signed, optional state_model, with the first leaf most significant. Nested fixed list leaves use indexed paths. Widths/ranges are JSON numbers and signed flags retain numeric zero/one; absence of a state model does not invent one. The shared closed shape is advertised by schedule_report_interface_ports and source_optional_fields.interface_ports. T1983/T1984 qualify detached values, invalid shapes and declaration ownership; T2014/T2016/T2033/T2034 qualify actual record source and full native/API/newline reports. T2035 qualifies atomic HDL profile refusal and T2036 finite predecessor preservation. Record metadata is not inferred hardware or a writer-safety/runtime certificate; field writers, generated outputs and full consumer signoff retain their separate boundaries.

Reset provenance records ISF clause presence separately from resolved hardware: reset_provenance is an authored-order array of {domain, origin} entries, or null when a caller-created actor has no parser evidence. A legacy actor has null domain and origin explicit or legacy_default; named domains have their name and origin explicit or domain_absent. This does not prove grounding in an external specification or defer reset policy to instantiation. Explicit clause presence does not mean optional kind/polarity operands were authored. Successful directly parsed ISF check and semantic reports expose the same array as optional source.reset_provenance; failure reports and direct FSM inputs do not acquire it. Effective reset fields, scheduled FSM and HDL are unchanged. Native/API/newline equality, domain scope and malformed-evidence controls are qualified by T1978. Discovery lives in the schedule contract’s schedule_report_reset_provenance and the shared source contract’s optional_fields.reset_provenance, also projected as source_optional_fields in both public report contracts.

Reset clauses accept exactly one scalar name or list. A list may select one sync/async timing and one active_low/active_high polarity, in either order. Unknown, nested, repeated or conflicting options and extra operands are source errors in ordinary and strict modes. Successful provenance is not emitted for those failures; T1979 qualifies complete native/API/newline diagnostic equality and schedule refusal while T1978 preserves valid-source reports and HDL.

Actor-level passive observation metadata is report-only. The accepted source form is (observe NAME (role passive_monitor) (signals SIG...)), where SIG... must name public actor interface signals in a single-clock actor. The sibling VHDL verification-output mode is --emit-verification-output vhdl-observation-package --verification-outdir DIR source.isf, with artifacts under DIR/vhdl/ and the same DIR/verification-output-manifest.json manifest. Downstream tools may inspect the inert observation constants and manifest metadata, but they must not treat the artifact as a VHDL syntax/compile/PSL/simulation/formal/analyzer result or as scoreboard, coverage, reusable VIP, direct IAL2, schedule JSON, check JSON, or semantic JSON behavior.

The capability manifest’s verification_outputs discovery metadata is exact: both manifest_contract.top_level_section_presence_key_map and the section’s own public_top_level_presence_keys include every live top-level field, including guidance and json_safe_when_embedded_in_public_manifest. Downstream consumers should use either advertised list rather than maintaining a payload-key exception.

Direct .ppif verification-output generation is intentionally not selected for the current lane. IAL2 sources remain reviewable through generated .isf before generated .fsm; future protocol-specific checker, scoreboard, coverage, or VIP work must first define how PPIF facts annotate or lower into generated IAL1 verification metadata unless a later exact task-tree owner proves that a direct IAL2 route is required.

  • t/1255-isf-schedule-report-golden-matrix.t is the executable matrix for the advertised schedule-report branches.
  • Each matrix case runs through both FSM::Scheduler::ISF->report(...) and ./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json, and the test requires equal payloads.
  • Every advertised schedule_report_* contract branch has a matrix owner where that branch is a schedule-report payload family.
  • schedule_report_full_schema_stable is true for schedule JSON schema_version: 1.

  • Raw assignment provenance, private assignment indexes, and activation proof internals are not public schedule-report fields.
  • Public substitutes are bounded summaries: compile_issues[] source summaries, compatible_fanin_groups[], priority_resolutions[], resource_arbitration[], transaction_port_bindings[], bank_accesses[], and aggregate counts such as dt_blocks[].assignments.
  • Parent reports do not embed recursive child schedule reports. Public multi-file detail is the lower(...) files map, generated .fsm artifacts, actor_network, generated_composition, library_uses[], and clock_domains[] / crossings[].
  • Downstream integrations should report bugs with the runnable source, command, bundle, and observed output. They do not need to classify whether a failure belongs to .fsm, .isf, private provenance, or generated child internals.

Scalar summaries:

  • schema_version: integer 1 for the current schedule-report payload shape. This is separate from the embedding.isf_public_interface.schema_version contract metadata.
  • source: report source basename derived from the actor name with .isf.
  • scheduled_fsm: scheduled .fsm basename for the report scope. Multi-domain reports use the generated <actor>_top.fsm artifact.
  • clock: actor/default-domain clock name; omitted legacy single-clock clocks report clk.
  • reset: object with name, kind, and polarity for configured or defaulted legacy single-clock resets; null only when the selected default-domain reset is omitted in a (clock-domains ...) actor.
  • watchdog: scalar watchdog limit; omitted watchdogs report 65535; accepted actor-level actor constants, actor scalar parameters, and qualified imported package scalar constants report as resolved integers.
  • inputs, outputs, port_count, state_count: non-negative integer counts. Multi-domain generated-top reports use state_count == 0 and put domain-local counts in clock_domains[].
  • compile_issues: array; empty on successful reports without nonfatal issues.

15. Diagnostics And Fail-Closed Policy

FSMGen must reject unsupported or malformed public ISF forms before emitting misleading scheduled artifacts. Downstream tools should surface diagnostics as source errors and should not assume a malformed form was partially accepted.

Operand-contract failures after CLI lowering preserve the authored ISF path in the report and embedded source context, including registered generated domain children. Explicit --outdir retention does not change that origin; directly checking a retained FSM uses its physical path. Public check/semantic API and MCP queries preserve the same failure reason without backend module/method prefixes. This source mapping is file-level, not a line/column source map.

Required fail-closed examples:

  • Unknown actor, transaction, rule, drive, storage, domain, or resource names where a declaration is required.

  • Duplicate singleton actor clauses.

  • Duplicate names in interfaces, drives, storage, rules, transactions, parameters, domains, imports, or instances.

  • Unsupported transaction clause heads in a lowered context.

  • Unsupported (on ...) body forms such as (params ...).

  • Rule triggers targeting unknown transactions.

  • Direct/local rule-trigger output bindings.

  • Literal-zero, actor-constant-zero, actor-parameter-zero, and same-transaction-parameter-zero divisor operands in shipped runtime division/modulo expression contexts.

  • Watchdog limits that name actor-level transaction parameters, nested-control-flow transaction parameters, cross-transaction parameters, runtime interface signals, unknown symbolic names, arbitrary expressions, constants that resolve to zero, actor/transaction parameters that resolve to zero or non-scalar values, or distinct per-await limits in one transaction.

  • Repeat counts that name cross-transaction parameters, unknown symbolic names, arbitrary expressions, malformed scalar tokens, actor/transaction parameters that resolve to non-scalar values, runtime names without width evidence, or statically zero bodies containing malformed child activation subclause syntax.

  • Latency min/max bounds that name cross-transaction parameters, runtime interface signals, unknown symbolic names, arbitrary expressions, constants that resolve to zero, or actor/transaction parameters that resolve to zero or non-scalar values.

  • Generated child activation overrides that change child transaction parameters consumed by repeat, wait, latency, or top-level await-local watchdog lowering. Same-value overrides are accepted; mismatches fail closed until per-activation static timing specialization is shipped.

  • Generated child activation overrides that change child transaction parameters consumed by data-operation widths (shift_left, shift_right, assemble, extract). Same-value overrides are accepted; mismatches fail closed with a targeted static-width parameter diagnostic until per-activation data-op width specialization is shipped.

  • Generated child activation overrides that change child transaction parameters consumed by transaction port widths ((ports (input/output NAME (width PARAM)))). Same-value overrides are accepted; mismatches fail closed with a targeted static port-width parameter diagnostic until per-activation transaction port width specialization is shipped.

  • Cross-domain repeat-body do: a (do TARGET (domain X)) annotation where the target transaction is in a different clock domain than the calling transaction now fails closed with a targeted “cross-domain repeat-body do remains deferred” diagnostic instead of the generic same-domain-feature (params) requirement message. Cross-domain do without the (domain ...) annotation still emits the generic clock-domain violation message. Cross-domain repeat-body do lowering itself remains backlog.

  • Temporal contract windows that need activation-site override-specialized lowering beyond same-value generated child activation overrides, transaction parameters from other transactions, runtime interface signals, unknown symbolic names, arbitrary expressions, unknown or unqualified package constants, aggregate package constants, package member/item paths, ambiguous local-enum/package-constant spellings, constants that resolve to zero, or actor/transaction parameters that resolve to zero or non-scalar values.

  • Direct cross-domain access without a shipped crossing primitive.

  • Width mismatch where width evidence is known.

  • Parameter override unknown names, duplicate names, symbolic values, and incompatible aggregate/list shapes.

This document is the human integration contract. The manifest is the exact JSON-safe discovery object for automated checks. If they disagree, treat that as a documentation bug and update them in the same slice.

18. Deferred Or Non-Public Surface

The following are not public shipped integration surfaces today:

  • Full raw parser actor hash as a stable API.
  • Full LoweringIR as a stable API.
  • Full schedule JSON schema beyond the advertised key families.
  • Textual include semantics for libraries.
  • Standalone transaction or drive library exports.
  • Broader interface, transaction-port, storage width, or bank-depth expressions beyond actor-local scalar parameter defaults and the shipped qualified package-scalar-constant actor interface width and actor-owned scalar storage width, actor-owned bank storage width, and actor-owned bank storage depth subsets.
  • Derived parameter expressions and package/imported constants outside the shipped qualified actor parameter, generated-child transaction parameter default, generated activation override, reusable-library use-site override, actor interface width, actor-owned scalar storage width, actor-owned bank storage width, and actor-owned bank storage depth scalar-constant subsets.
  • Record output member writes, generated whole-output handoff mappings and output native runtime qualification; root-list actor ports and aggregate transaction ports. Selected packed record actor input runtime is qualified in SystemVerilog, but X/Z behavior, reset-free initialization and full aggregate-interface consumer signoff are not established.
  • General memory-array HDL emission for actor-owned banks.
  • Arbitrary CDC, payload CDC, reset CDC, level sampling across domains, or FIFO-like cross-domain storage.
  • Direct cross-domain reads/writes/triggers/activations/bindings.
  • Direct/local rule-trigger output bindings.
  • Direct (on ...) activation parameter overrides.
  • Snapshot-vs-live binding timing selection beyond the shipped binding timing.
  • Proof that every dynamic division/modulo divisor is nonzero. Literal-zero, actor-constant-zero, actor-parameter-zero, and same-transaction-parameter-zero divisors are rejected, but arbitrary runtime scalar nonzero proof and use-site-specialized parameter divisor proof are not public shipped surfaces yet.
  • A formal frozen EBNF grammar artifact or JSON Schema artifact. This document and the manifest are the current integration contract; a machine grammar or schema should be produced by a future task if required.

19. Integration Guidance

For a downstream producer:

  • Emit only the source forms listed in this document.
  • If FSMGen behavior looks wrong, follow the strict, format-agnostic reproduction bundle flow in docs/DOWNSTREAM_ISSUE_REPORTING.md. Do not guess whether the root cause is source syntax, lowering, reporting, HDL, or public API behavior; provide the exact FSMGen-facing artifacts and command transcript.
  • Prefer explicit scalar names and explicit widths.
  • Use transaction ports and (bind ...) for runtime-varying data.
  • Use (params ...) only for static specialization on generated activation forms that explicitly support it.
  • Use actor constants or actor-local scalar parameter defaults for static generated activation parameter override values.
  • Use actor constants, actor-local scalar parameter defaults, or qualified imported package scalar constants for static latency bound symbols.
  • Use actor constants, actor-local scalar parameter defaults, or qualified imported package scalar constants for static temporal-contract window symbols.
  • Use actor constants, actor-local scalar parameter defaults, or qualified imported package scalar constants for static actor-level watchdog limits.
  • Use actor constants, actor-local scalar parameter defaults, same-transaction scalar parameter defaults, or qualified imported package scalar constants for static top-level await-local watchdog limits.
  • Use actor constants, actor-local scalar parameter defaults, or qualified imported package scalar constants for static wait-count symbols.
  • Treat every fail-closed diagnostic as a source-generation bug.
  • Use --emit-schedule-json in tests to confirm schedule/report shape.
  • Use --check --json or --check-json when a downstream workflow needs a machine-readable pass/fail result. For .isf inputs, parser, lowering, schedule-report, and downstream semantic check failures exit nonzero while still emitting success: false JSON to stdout with the diagnostic message in diagnostics[0].message.
  • Use generated .fsm as the human review artifact before HDL.
  • Use --capability-manifest to check the current bounded public contract.

For a downstream analyzer:

  • Consume schedule JSON key families listed here.
  • Preserve unknown keys for forward compatibility.
  • Do not depend on raw Perl object internals.
  • Do not infer support from parser-carried private clause payloads.
  • Treat compile_issues[] as nonfatal warnings on successful reports.
  • Treat missing artifacts or diagnostics as integration failures, not partial success. Empty stdout from --check --json for an existing .isf input is a reportable FSMGen bug, not an expected downstream contract.

ISF Types, Enums, And Aggregates

This chapter is the review surface for the shipped .isf type, enum, and aggregate subset. It describes what authors may write today, what the scheduled .fsm review artifact preserves, and what still fails closed.

The important rule is that ISF does not own a separate type system. Local (types ...) and (enums ...) declarations, package imports, scalar aliases, enum members, and packed aggregate aliases reuse the same .fsm declaration and package machinery that direct .fsm roots already use.

Declarations And Imports

Actor-local declarations are written in the actor body. Schematic shape (the actor body continues with (interface ...) and one or more (transaction ...) clauses):

(actor typed_actor
  (types
    (type byte (bits 8))
    (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit)))
    (type lanes_t (list bit (bits 2))))
  (enums
    (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  ...)

Existing .fsm package roots can be imported by name:

(actor package_typed_actor
  (imports
    (package shared))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  ...)

The scheduled .fsm preserves these declarations as review artifacts:

(+import shared)
(+types
  (type byte (bits 8))
  (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit))))
(+enums
  (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))

Imported package roots are embedded into the scheduled .fsm output so CLI HDL generation remains self-contained even when the lowerer uses a temporary scheduled .fsm path.

Scalar Type Aliases

Width-bearing declarations may use (type NAME) instead of (width N) when NAME resolves to a scalar alias.

(interface
  (input data (type byte))
  (output mode_out (type shared.mode_bits)))

(transaction tx
  (ports
    (input payload (type byte)))
  ...)

(storage
  (var scratch (type byte)))

NAME may be actor-local (byte) or package-qualified (shared.mode_bits). (width N) and (type NAME) are mutually exclusive on the same declaration. Unknown aliases fail before lowering.

Aggregate Storage Carriers

Packed list and record aliases are accepted on actor-owned storage variables. Packed records also support actor input ports, as described below.

Record-output declarations and exact-type whole copies are now source-admitted. Their complete public/generated/backend execution qualification remains open. The mandatory scheduler gate applies the qualified conservative writer rules to each actual bound module before publishing a schedule or scheduled .fsm; a multi-domain actor is checked through its separate owning domain modules. The preparatory inventory matches each resolved output declaration to its actual module port and joins every write to its packed range, explicit source owner and activation conditions. A whole output overlaps each of its members; different members may be disjoint. Repeated states of one controller and independent controllers require different admission evidence. Equal values, entry conditions and an empty legacy conflict report do not establish exclusion. Local/imported nested layouts, rule/drive writers and actual domain modules are qualified for inventory. Its private admission consumer now accepts a sole writer or ordinary <- assignments in different states of one explicitly owned transaction controller, together with disjoint physical targets. Overlapping independent writers, duplicate writes in one active state or DT, and timed operators have no inferred compatibility or exclusion. Caller-supplied filtered writer lists are refused. The private inventory can inspect unresolved writer combinations; public scheduling and emission must pass admission. Generated output mappings remain closed until their handoff mapping is qualified. See the inventory evidence. The admission evidence retains the bounded rules and counterexamples. Independent-controller runtime reachability remains governed by its separate repair and qualification tasks.

Output-only and mixed record contexts now have their mandatory preparatory source gates. Whole copies require the same resolved record type. Scalar samples preserve the leaf’s width, signedness and state model in a private alias; they cannot replace an existing declaration. Output record fields retain their owning clock domain, so a read in another domain requires an explicit crossing. The source policy keeps output member writes closed while preserving scalar output slices and the prepared type toolkit’s member facts. These checks now guard authored output declarations and whole copies; they do not qualify output execution. See the source-context evidence.

The shared HDL profile guard also applies to authored record outputs. Unsupported verilog/v and vhdl requests name the actor, output and authored type and recommend systemverilog. Mixed Verilog interfaces preserve the existing input diagnostic priority. The old input-only helper retains its contract, and target-neutral schedule preview stays available. Actual local, imported, aliased, mixed and unused output sources now qualify the same normal native/facade refusals, complete machine error products and atomic destinations. SystemVerilog and its sv alias retain complete supported native HDL text apart from date banners; these generation checks do not establish runtime support. See the actual target-profile evidence. See the profile evidence.

A whole copy can publish actor-owned storage through a declared record output:

(actor record_output_example
 (clock clk)
 (types (type frame (record (tag (bits 2)) (payload (bits 3)))))
 (interface (input start) (output packet (type frame)) (output done))
 (storage (var held (type frame)))
 (transaction main
  (on start)
  (set held.tag 1)
  (set held.payload 5)
  (set packet held)
  (complete done)))

The output keeps the existing type alias and packing. Output-to-storage and output-to-output whole copies are also permitted when their complete resolved record types match and declared roles allow the read/write. Matching width alone is insufficient. Scalar output-field reads and explicit scalar captures retain the leaf’s exact type. Unused record-output declarations are accepted; undriven outputs promise no value. Typed output reset and default options, whole-record inferred captures and root-list/formal aggregates remain closed. Output member writes retain their separate qualification gate. Independent overlapping output writers refuse even with equal values, different entry guards or a priority declaration. Generated record-output mappings remain closed until their handoff qualification. This gate applies even when the record output is unused or the child uses only a scalar formal with the same name. Plain local do without generated children remains accepted. Actual spawned, parameterized blocking and owning-domain captures show that generated output reads need live owner views and whole writes need an owner update route. Both repairs precede publication; merely removing the gate would expose missing wiring. Scalar sibling schedules can succeed while strict check and semantic queries reject unconnected child ports. See the generated-output ingress.

The detached child read plan qualifies private typed data inputs, source-name masking and emitted operand rebasing, including record outputs named start and done. Production owner routes and output writer handoffs remain open. Entry when bodies now refuse unsupported actions rather than dropping them. First-operation conditional macro intent and scalar X/Z false-operand diagnosis still precede read integration; this preparation does not establish output execution or X/Z behavior. Actual local/imported/alias/mixed, reverse-copy and owning-domain carriers strictly replay; this establishes source and carrier admission, with execution still pending. See the source-integration evidence.

Native check and semantic reports return the successful authored declarations in source.interface_ports; schedule reports return interface_ports and clock_domains[].interface_ports for the selected domains. Inputs precede outputs, with authored order inside each role. Local, forward and imported aliases, mixed interfaces, reverse copies and unused outputs retain complete layouts and types through the in-process API and newline MCP tools. Signed and state-model facts remain explicit; absent state models stay absent. These public products are qualified separately from HDL execution. See the public-source evidence.

Save the example above as .artifacts/record-output-example.isf, then query it:

./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf
./bin/fsmgen --strict --emit-semantic-json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf
./bin/fsmgen --emit-schedule-json .artifacts/record-output-example.isf

A failed check or semantic query returns success: false and its contextual diagnostic, without successful declaration metadata or a partial semantic result. A failed schedule query publishes no schedule JSON; API/MCP retain their existing message-only error contract. Target-profile atomic qualification and the finite complete predecessor comparison are complete. Existing local/imported/shadowed/unused inputs, maintained scalar/storage examples and generated/domain input sources retain their complete public reports, strict carriers and SystemVerilog generation products. Only qualified repository/generated-lowering directory prefixes and date banners are normalized. Comparison evidence retains the full responses and failed capture controls. The maintained isf/record_output.isf now supplies a nested record/list input/storage/output example with signed/state metadata, a whole output copy and a scalar output-field read. Its feature.isf_record_output supported-smoke owner covers bounded source, reports, lowering and SystemVerilog generation. T2037 independently qualifies literal declaration/type/layout and corrupt-data refusal. Complete predecessor/ current catalog, all query cohort applicability and native/API/newline discovery are retained in the corpus receipt. Only the new entry and derived accounting change; all prior source hashes and metadata remain exact. This does not claim actual execution of every cohort row. Generated output mappings, field writes and execution remain separately gated.

(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t))
  (var lanes (type shared.lanes_t)))

The scheduled .fsm keeps the authored alias in typed +size review entries, and schedule reports expose the storage item with its packed width, authored type, and resolved type_kind (record or list).

Packed record actor inputs are admitted with (input NAME (type T)), where T is a local or package-qualified alias. Fields are live scalar reads in supported transaction conditions, set/update RHS values, rules and drives. Nested record members, list items and scalar slices use the existing packed layout. The first authored member occupies the most significant bits.

(actor record_input
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (signed (four_state (bits 5)))))))
 (interface (input start) (input packet (type frame))
  (output seen (width 5)) (output done))
 (storage (var held (type frame)))
 (transaction main
  (on start)
  (set held packet)
  (set seen packet.data)
  (complete done)))

The maintained example is record_input.isf. Run ./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json isf/record_input.isf from the repository root.

That example uses a local alias to an imported record. Its companion record_input_types.fsm declares the package:

(?pkg:record_input_types
  (+types
    (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (signed (four_state (bits 5))))))))

The actor imports it and retains its local spelling:

(imports (package record_input_types))
(types (type frame record_input_types.frame))

Local aliases and nested members may reference declared imported types. Imports resolve before local aliases; qualified names remain in their package namespace. Forward local aliases also work. Missing types and undeclared packages refuse. The scheduled carrier embeds the package root for independent strict replay. T2014 qualifies accepted nested/imported/nearest-shadow public sources; T2015 qualifies scalar and nested imported dependencies. T2016 qualifies contextual public refusals. T2017 qualifies the unchanged supplied SPECFORGE whole-copy and field-guard sources, the exact earlier storage-only products and complete public discovery. The supplied whole-copy source uses a sixteen-bit input: subtype occupies bits 15 through 12, payload bits 11 through 0. Its field guard reads that same layout. Frontend and generated/domain source, report and replay qualification is complete. Supported input backend and binary execution profiles are qualified below; complete output-dependent consumer delivery remains open.

Generated readers retain one typed packed input in their private interface. Reused instances receive the live actor input independently; an unread inherited input is omitted from the child while the authored top declaration remains. An input-to-storage copy keeps the register and its reset in the actor or domain owner. A sole generated writer supplies typed private write data and an explicit enable to that owner. Carrier checks establish structure and strict replay; the separate direct/generated observations below qualify their timing and reset behavior.

The runnable record_input_children.isf imports the same package and reuses a reader in domain io:

(transaction worker (domain io)
  (ports (output result (width 5)))
  (wait 2)
  (set result packet.data)
  (complete done))
(transaction main (domain io)
  (on start)
  (set held packet)
  (spawn worker as left (bind (output result seen)))
  (spawn worker as right (bind (output result again)))
  (await_all done)
  (complete done))

Run ./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json isf/record_input_children.isf. Its explicit top exposes the declared inputs and outputs, plus each domain’s clock and declared reset. unused stays in clock-only domain idle; packet, held and the readers belong to io. There is no implicit crossing or child register copy. T2019 independently qualifies local/imported nested aliases, reused readers, unused inputs and sole generated copies, including blocking calls. Ordinary composition children now retain their source’s embedded package context through the normal frontend; external children still resolve packages beside their own source. T2020 checks both boundaries.

Accepted generated/domain check, semantic and schedule queries are also qualified through the native CLI, adapter API and actual newline MCP. The complete products agree, including declared layouts and reset provenance. Clock-only siblings retain an absent reset; each realized reader keeps its owning clock and explicit reset contract. Contextual generated/domain refusals and prior-product closure are also qualified by T2021 and the execution reconciliation.

The semantic report distinguishes authored declarations from realized wiring:

Public locationMeaning
source.interface_portsAuthored record aliases, scalar leaf layout and declared domains.
semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.signal_analysisThe composition top’s physical vector pins.
semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.composition_children[].intent_hir.signal_analysisEach module’s typed input/output declarations, including declared_type_name and the complete declared_type_spec.
semantic.forward_ir.intent_hir.composition_children[].structural_rtl_ir.portsThe corresponding typed structural ports.
Schedule clock_domains[].interface_portsThe declarations owned by each domain, including unused inputs.

Join children using instance_name, module_name and source_name. Reused readers have distinct instance identities and retain the same declared type. Private write-data ports carry the target’s complete record type. Their presence does not add authored public pins or permit competing writers.

packet is one six-bit input; it does not become separate field pins. packet.flag occupies bit 5 and packet.data bits 4 through 0. The copy into held requires the same resolved recursive record type. Equivalent local or imported aliases may have different spellings; equal packed width alone is insufficient. Member names/order, nested shape, scalar kinds, signed properties and declared state models must match. An unspecified state model stays unspecified for this comparison. Existing storage-only copies keep their prior contract.

Use (sample packet.data as captured) in an already supported sample position when a snapshot is needed. The private scalar alias retains the leaf width, signed/state properties and existing capture timing. It adds no public port or implicit reset. Alias collisions, shared transaction writers and invalid sample paths refuse. Repeated captures by one owner preserve their existing rules.

Inputs cannot be assignment targets. Unknown members, out-of-range items, subaggregate scalar operands, whole-record conditions/arithmetic and whole-record sampling refuse. A nearest scalar formal or drive parameter masks an outer record. A scalar drive parameter cannot read or write record members, even while its width is unresolved, including member access after a scalar selector. Bare scalar values and scalar slices keep their existing width validation; enum/package names retain their namespace meaning. Named-domain reads and copies require the declared owning domain or a supported crossing. Generated child scalar outputs still require their published explicit bindings. Strict width checks require width-aligned scalar assignments.

A static bit or slice of a named-drive scalar parameter follows that parameter, including inside an expression. It does not read a same-named actor record. The existing bare-parameter assignment supplies the parameter width; a selector alone does not borrow a wider outer declaration. For example, whole establishes the five-bit parameter below, while seen receives its low four bits:

(actor scalar_drive_selectors
 (clock clk)
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (bits 5)))))
 (interface (input start) (input value (width 5)) (input packet (type frame))
  (output whole (width 5)) (output seen (width 4)) (output done))
 (drive (publish packet) (whole packet) (seen packet[3:0]))
 (transaction main (on start) (drive publish value) (complete done)))

The drive’s packet is scalar and masks the actor’s six-bit record. Its member access such as packet.data still refuses. The same parameter identity applies to an explicitly bound generated invocation and to the drive’s owning domain. Transaction locals retain their existing interface-name collision refusals.

A generated child’s scalar formal can share an actor record input name. In a binding, the formal name identifies the callee port; the actual value belongs to the caller. The binding below sends value to the child’s scalar packet:

(actor scalar_record_binding
 (clock clk) (reset (rst_n async active_low))
 (types (type frame (record (flag bit) (data (bits 5)))))
 (interface (input start) (input value (width 3)) (input packet (type frame))
  (output observed (width 3)) (output done))
 (transaction worker (ports (input packet (width 3)) (output result (width 3)))
  (set result packet[2:0]) (complete done))
 (transaction main (on start)
  (spawn worker as job (bind (input packet value) (output result observed)))
  (await_all done) (complete done)))

The child keeps its scalar public port and selector. The actor record keeps its own type, width and domain; no automatic record connection is added. Transaction targets, instance labels and static parameter/domain/timing names also retain their identity roles. Existing endpoint, width, timing and domain checks still apply. This does not admit record input roots or field reads as binding actuals: (input packet actor_record) and (input packet (+ actor_record.data 0)) remain refused. Bare slices are outside the existing signal/literal/list-expression binding grammar; this repair does not introduce another binding form.

Rejected check and semantic queries retain their complete failure reports and nullable diagnostic codes, without successful declarations or partial semantic payloads. Schedule failure emits no schedule JSON. Its API and newline transport retain the existing message-only error contract; the compiler diagnostic appears in native stderr. None of these queries modifies the source or imported package.

Schedule preview reports scheduled intent before HDL realization. A later composition wiring refusal, such as an unbound generated child output, can therefore retain a complete schedule preview while strict check and semantic queries refuse. Use those strict queries to qualify the realized composition; a schedule preview alone does not prove its ports are connected.

Public report qualification checks complete JSON primitive kinds, source bytes, named producers and fixed scalar/storage controls. Historical compatibility comparisons permit only independently qualified additive metadata, exact source relocation and emitted date banners. HDL execution remains separately qualified.

Record output declarations and exact-type whole copies are source-admitted under SEM .60.4.3.3.4.3. Output member writes, root-list actor ports, transaction-local aggregate ports, aggregate banks and variants remain deferred. Bounded output public/profile/corpus reconciliation .3.4.4 is complete. Generated/backend execution qualification .3.5 remains open. Whole-root and member writes must be compared by their packed ranges and actual owners; an empty conflict report does not establish compatibility. No implicit arbitration is added. Output-field admission remains the next separate lane. The compiler preserves typed +size, explicit +interface, exact declaration metadata and private sample carriers. Generated/domain source, carrier and complete public qualification includes current catalog declarations, full discovery, contextual refusals and fixed scalar/storage compatibility controls. Supported input backend profiles and packed binary behavior are independently qualified below. Supplied output-dependent consumer signoff remains separate work. The direct public-pin behavioral witness is executed and qualified for both emitted Verilog families. It checks packed layout, entry sampling, live reads, whole-copy timing, held values, idle holds, repeated requests and asynchronous reset/abort. Its independently authored source and bench change the input around public phase outputs. The data member is signed and five bits wide:

RequestEntry-sampled dataWhole-copy dataLater live dataPrior held data
First7-13-3-14
Repeated-295-13
After reset/abort3-8-15-14

These independent literals distinguish each read/copy edge; outputs retain their assigned values while idle. An actually compiled source with the same width but an unsigned data member reaches the bench’s signed-comparison rejection. Complete original stage results, source identities, bounds and cleanup are retained in the sealed observation. Generated/domain public-pin behavior is also qualified for the named-domain source and ordinary blocking source in both emitted Verilog families. Both use the table’s independently literal entry/copy/live/prior words, reuse live reader instances and give the packed register one generated copier. Parent-owned phase outputs separate input changes: the bench requires the copied scalar result during phase 1 before phase 2, then checks every copied packed leaf and later live reads. Spawned scalar bindings forward the child’s retained output; the parameterized blocking binding is valid during child completion and defaults to zero afterward. The bench checks that distinction again at parent completion and idle.

Repeated requests, sampled/prior-held values, owning asynchronous reset/abort and idle hold pass. The named source retains an unused clock-only sibling; changing its input/clock and stopping/restarting that clock do not disturb owned values. This establishes no initial-state guarantee for reset-free hardware. The actually compiled unsigned counterexample passes its copied result observation, then reaches the expected signed-comparison rejection. Complete original results, source/producer identities, stage bounds and cleanup are retained in the complete generated observation.

The first compile exposed an illegal typed wire containing two-state members; the carrier now preserves the same packed typedef on a variable declaration. A subsequent blocking test used the wrong late-retention expectation; its completion-window correction preserves all packed-storage predicates. Both diagnoses, exact predecessor controls and original partial receipts remain tracked. SEM .60.4.3.2.5.4.4 completes generated execution reconciliation: current public reports, contextual refusals, package integration and prior scalar/domain-storage contracts pass, with complete typed native/API/newline products and unchanged source/producers. Backend profiles .5.5.1 retain the precise VHDL refusals below. Final public/corpus reconciliation .5.5.2 qualifies supplied sources, complete discovery, current catalog and JSON kinds, preserving the unchanged full-cohort and prior evidence. Independent input signoff .5.5.3.2.3 closes the selected input portions of R1–R3 against their exact source, public, profile and original native evidence. Record-output execution and field writers, complete SPECFORGE aggregate delivery, X/Z behavior and historical native causality remain separate obligations.

Record-input HDL support is qualified separately for each backend. The direct, generated and named-domain witnesses above execute in both Verilog families. The VHDL scaffold refuses these record-input profiles: the mixed signed/two-state fixture identifies an unsupported packed member, the supplied whole-copy and field-guard fixtures identify their typed input declaration, and the generated tops identify their unsupported composition shape. Failure returns no successful pipeline product, creates no new HDL destination and preserves an existing one. Scalar VHDL inputs and the previously supported inferred packed-output fixtures remain supported. Their file emission does not establish VHDL analyzer or runtime qualification; see the backend boundary.

For example, this supplied input is accepted by the frontend but its VHDL generation refuses the typed lmp_in input:

./bin/fsmgen --strict --quiet --language vhdl --output .artifacts/record-input.vhd docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/record-port.isf

Use systemverilog for the qualified record-input HDL profile. HDL requests for these ISF record inputs now refuse verilog and its v alias, naming the actor, input and declared type and recommending systemverilog. They preserve an existing destination and publish no new or partial HDL product. Source parsing, declaration metadata and schedule preview remain target-neutral. The historical verilog emitter observation retained packed SystemVerilog typedefs in these fixtures. The record-input behavior observations compiled both emitter options as .sv sources with Verilator’s default SystemVerilog parser. They establish those recorded binary behaviors, but do not qualify IEEE 1364 Verilog-2005 syntax. The version-matched Verilator contract defines the default parser and separate language selectors. SEM .5.5.3.2.2 qualifies the precise current profile refusal and preserves complete SystemVerilog HDL against the predecessor apart from date banners. The historical two-emitter native archives remain immutable. Current T2024/T2025 preparation targets SystemVerilog; any new native execution requires fresh observer qualification. T2027 retains the precise CLI/public-pipeline refusals, destination preservation, supported controls and false-success/wrong-diagnostic counterexamples.

Run the authored source checks from the repository root:

./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json t/data/isf_record_input_generated_domains_runtime.isf
./bin/fsmgen --strict --check --json t/data/isf_record_input_generated_blocking_runtime.isf

Binary-valued Verilator execution does not establish four-state X/Z behavior; signed/state declarations and execution claims are qualified separately. See 0113 and declared interface metadata. Existing declaration-collision refusals still apply.

Single-member records and single-item lists also preserve their aggregate identity. Nested forms and forward local aliases work in actor declarations and survive the scheduled .fsm replay. For example:

(actor single_payload
  (types
    (type payload_t (list (record (payload byte_t))))
    (type byte_t (bits 8)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input data (width 8))
    (output result (width 8)))
  (storage (var value (type payload_t) (reset 0)))
  (transaction main
    (on start)
    (set value data)
    (set result value)))

Here the storage keeps its nested list/record shape while whole-value transfers use the packed representation. Empty aggregates, missing member types, duplicate field names, unknown aliases, and dependency cycles fail during type resolution. Generated transaction children in ordinary/single-domain actors read these same owner-held values through typed internal connections; they do not allocate private copies. Whole-value reads use the packed representation, and scalar leaf reads retain their exact leaf width. For example:

(actor aggregate_child_read
  (clock clk) (reset (rst_n async active_low))
  (types (type status_t (record (payload (bits 7)) (flag bit))))
  (interface (input start) (input data (width 8))
             (output observed (width 7)) (output done))
  (storage (var status (type status_t) (reset 0)))
  (transaction worker
    (ports (output result (width 7)))
    (wait 4) (set result status.payload) (complete done))
  (transaction parent
    (on start)
    (spawn worker as w0 (bind (output result observed)))
    (wait 1) (set status data)
    (await_all done) (complete done)))

The worker observes the owner’s later payload value. The public ports stay scalar; the generated child receives the aggregate root with its type intact. See Composition for reset ownership, live-read timing and the remaining domain/write boundaries.

Enum Values

Enum members may be local, such as mode.BUSY, or package-qualified, such as shared.mode.BUSY. The parser resolves them before lowering in static specialization contexts and preserves authored tokens in review contexts where the scheduled .fsm can carry them directly.

Enum members in expression operator position remain rejected. Enum member targets also remain rejected because enum members are constants, not writable storage or output names. Unsupported enum references fail before scheduled .fsm emission with diagnostics that name the unsupported context.

Enum names are not type aliases

An (enums (NAME ...)) declaration establishes only the enum member-value family NAME. It does not also establish a scalar type alias named NAME. Writing (type NAME) on a width-bearing interface port, transaction port, or storage variable when only (enums (NAME ...)) is declared fails closed:

(actor enum_not_a_type
  (enums (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output state_out (type mode))   ;; <-- ERROR: unknown type 'mode'
    (output done))
  ...)

Error: actor 'enum_not_a_type' interface port 'state_out' references unknown type 'mode'

To use an enum name as a width-bearing type, co-declare a backing scalar type alias (types (type NAME (bits k))) alongside (enums (NAME ...)). Co-declaring the same NAME in both (types ...) and (enums ...) is accepted and is the intended mechanism — they are distinct declaration roles (the (type) provides the width alias used by (type NAME); the (enums) provides the member values used by mode.BUSY-style references), so this is not a redeclaration conflict:

(actor enum_with_type
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (types (type mode (bits 1)))
  (enums (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1)))
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output state_out (type mode))
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (complete done)))

The backing (bits k) width is the author’s assertion and is not cross-validated against enum member magnitudes — (type mode (bits 1)) is accepted even with a member value that needs more bits. A downstream emitter recovering a dense 0..N-1 enum should choose k = ceil(log2(member_count)).

Actor-local (types ...), (enums ...), and (constants ...) declarations need not be referenced to be contract-valid: an unreferenced declaration lowers cleanly and is preserved in the corresponding scheduled .fsm review section.

Aggregate Leaf Values

Aggregate member and item paths are valid only when the root is a declared actor-owned aggregate storage variable and the path resolves to a scalar leaf.

(storage
  (var frame (type frame_t))
  (var lanes (type lanes_t)))

Valid scalar leaves include record members such as frame.flag and list items such as lanes[1]. Unknown record members, out-of-range list indexes, malformed paths, and paths that resolve to a whole record/list fail before lowering.

Aggregate paths in expression operator position remain rejected. Subaggregate operands, subaggregate updates, whole-record/whole-list truthiness, record-output member writes and root-list interface ports, transaction-local aggregate ports, aggregate storage banks, aggregate field/slice/update lowering beyond scalar leaves, and broader shape inference remain backlog.

Diagnostics

The parser resolves type aliases, enum members, and aggregate paths before scheduled .fsm emission. That means these failures are reported in ISF space:

  • Unknown local or package type aliases.
  • (width ...) and (type ...) on the same declaration.
  • Aggregate aliases on unsupported carriers.
  • Unknown enum families or enum members.
  • Enum references in unsupported contexts, including operator position or LHS target position.
  • Unknown aggregate record members.
  • Out-of-range aggregate list indexes.
  • Aggregate paths that resolve to whole records or lists where a scalar leaf is required.
  • Aggregate paths outside the shipped scalar leaf contexts listed above.

Strict HDL generation is part of the shipped contract for the listed forms.

When a form is accepted, the scheduled .fsm review artifact is the source of truth for how the ISF syntax reached the backend.

Aggregate Package Constants Fail Closed

A qualified imported package constant pkg.NAME works only when NAME is a scalar entry. Aggregate or member paths (pkg.AGG.member, pkg.LIST.idx, etc.) fail closed across every shipped consumer with a remains deferred diagnostic naming the consumer axis. The rejected source shape is a package whose constant is an aggregate, paired with an actor that reaches into a member path:

;; in a sibling shared.fsm file:
(?pkg:shared
  (+constants
    (CONFIG ((lat 4) (depth 8)))))

;; in the actor:
(transaction worker
  (on start)
  (wait shared.CONFIG.lat)        ;; <-- aggregate/member path
  (complete done))

The validator emits Transaction 'worker': wait count package constant 'shared.CONFIG' aggregate/member path 'shared.CONFIG.lat' remains deferred; wait counts accept only qualified package scalar constants in this slice. The same remains deferred phrase fires from the matching axis-specific helper for repeat counts, latency bounds, watchdog limits, contract windows, data-operation widths, activation parameter overrides, actor parameter defaults, and transaction parameter defaults. The deferred lane is aggregate/member-path resolution against the constant-symbol table; until it ships, authors must pre-resolve the member to a scalar pkg.CONSTANT (for example (+constants (CONFIG_LAT 4))) or use a same-transaction constant or parameter default instead.

Complete Accept-Path Examples

The chapter so far has shown schematic forms and table entries. The actors below are self-contained, copy-pasteable fixtures that each exercise one of the shipped type/enum/aggregate axes.

Scalar type alias

(actor type_alias_demo
  (types
    (type byte (bits 8)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (input data (type byte))
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start
      (sample data as captured))
    (wait 2)
    (complete done)))

Walkthrough. (types (type byte (bits 8))) declares one actor-local scalar alias byte resolving to an 8-bit value. (input data (type byte)) uses that alias in place of (width 8), which keeps the authored intent (byte) visible in the scheduled .fsm +size review entries. The transaction samples the input into local register captured at entry, waits two cycles, and completes. The lowered FSM carries the alias as a typed +size entry rather than a raw width.

Local enum

(actor enum_demo
  (enums
    (mode (IDLE 0) (BUSY 1) (DONE 2)))
  (constants
    (DEFAULT_STATE mode.IDLE))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (wait 4)
    (complete done)))

Walkthrough. (enums (mode ...)) declares one enum family mode with three members. Enum members are addressed dot-qualified (mode.IDLE, mode.BUSY, mode.DONE). (constants (DEFAULT_STATE mode.IDLE)) uses the enum-member token as a constant value: the authored mode.IDLE is preserved in the scheduled .fsm +constants and actor_constants[] entries while the resolved integer is available internally for static comparisons and waits. The transaction itself is the minimal on/wait/complete skeleton — the enum only contributes review metadata in this example.

Aggregate storage carrier

(actor aggregate_storage_demo
  (types
    (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit))))
  (storage
    (var frame (type frame_t)))
  (clock clk)
  (reset rst_n)
  (interface
    (input start)
    (output done))
  (transaction tx
    (on start)
    (wait 2)
    (complete done)))

Walkthrough. (type frame_t (record (mode (bits 2)) (flag bit))) declares a packed record alias with two members. (storage (var frame (type frame_t))) declares one actor-owned scalar storage frame whose width comes from the packed sum (2 + 1 = 3 bits). Packed record aliases are also admitted on actor input/output ports under the bounded record-port contracts above. Output member writes, root-list actor ports and transaction aggregate ports remain deferred. The scheduled .fsm keeps the alias frame_t in typed +size entries and the schedule report exposes the storage item with its packed width, authored type, and resolved type_kind (record).

ISF Shipped Feature Matrix

This chapter is the book-facing checklist for the .isf surface that is currently shipped. It does not replace the detailed chapters, the live spec, or the downstream handoff. It gives reviewers one place to confirm which feature families are supported, where to find examples, and where the explicit backlog boundary starts.

A feature is “shipped” here only when the source shape, scheduled .fsm lowering, runtime meaning, diagnostics, reports or review artifacts, and focused regression evidence exist. Parser acceptance alone is not a support claim.

Requested Extensions And Current Gaps

SPECFORGE’s configuration, verification and phase-membership requests are owned implementation work; they are not shipped capabilities yet.

AreaCurrent boundaryRequested extension
Parameter-sized portsWidth references resolve to the default; an emitted HDL parameter does not make the port generic.Preserve width dependencies through HDL and supported instance overrides.
Parameter constraintsScalar parameters carry defaults without declared legal or recommended sets.Check legal values/ranges at defaults and overrides; report constraints and advisory recommendations.
Optional interfacesZero widths are rejected; the unsupported present option is rejected.Explicit presence, absent-input values and supported per-instance specialization.
Actor invariantsVerification checks are written inside transactions; their existing meaning is always-on.Actor-level assert/assume/cover, including actors without transactions.
Known-value checksknown and isunknown are unsupported.Verification-only knownness with independent X/Z behavior evidence.
Physical-time durationsTiming bounds use cycle counts; clocks carry signal identity without a declared rate.Exact duration conversion against a declared frequency/period, authored-duration and derived-cycle reports, and counter-based duration waits while preserving existing cycle-count behavior. Owned by SEM .60.1; not shipped.
Named timersTransaction watchdog expiry is an error path; named actor timers and distinct per-await limits are refused.Concurrent actor-owned timers with start/restart/stop, ordinary expiry conditions and schedule metadata. Cycle limits are required; duration limits follow duration support. Distinct per-await watchdog limits are optional. Owned by SEM .60.2; not shipped.
Record interface portsLocal/imported packed actor record inputs, live scalar field reads and exact-type input-to-storage copies are admitted. Frontend/generated/domain source, carriers and complete public products are qualified; direct/generated binary behavior passes both emitter options with SystemVerilog parsing. Current ISF Verilog and selected VHDL profiles refuse precisely. Selected input delivery is qualified; full output-dependent consumer delivery remains open.Record outputs and exact-type whole copies now have bounded source/carrier admission with conservative physical writer checks; bounded public source/profile/corpus products are qualified; generated/execution qualification and output member writes remain open. Root-list ports and variants are optional. The complete request is owned by SEM .60.4 and is not finished.
Transaction phase groupsMembership cannot be carried as checked transaction metadata.Checked phase/member/role facts without invented values, order or behavior.

Unknown or malformed interface-port options are rejected in default and strict modes through native/API/MCP queries. This validation boundary does not add optional-port support. Declared inputs and outputs now retain their interface roles even when unused or undriven. Output preservation adds no value assignment. An explicitly reset output without a data writer now resets and holds under the module hardware-reset contract. Its semantic drive family has no data-driver blocks. Inspect realized semantic/HDL interfaces and behavior when evaluating presence or reset semantics.

The earlier derived-width request depends on genuine generic-width support; it is distinct from it. Exact request scopes, repair order, current reproductions and bounded owners are recorded in SPECFORGE feedback response, including its current delivery status and complete unstated-reset answer. Reset omission selects the documented legacy default; a clock-only domain means no reset, without guaranteed initialization. No current form defers reset policy to instantiation.

Status Vocabulary

StatusMeaning

Repeat-body activation matrix note: the shipped nested-repeat activation shapes under top-level when and switch branches are described by construction, not by an exhaustive list of spellings. The accepted context is a repeat directly inside a top-level branch body. The accepted activation kinds are local do, generated-child do, generated do with static (params ...), that generated do with (bind ...) handoffs, and that generated do with optional bind handoffs plus same-domain metadata.

The lifetime rule is the same for every accepted spelling: a blocking do must observe its own fresh done handoff, generated-top parameter/binding handoffs stay scoped to that generated do instance, declared same-domain metadata records ownership without adding CDC, and every pending generated-spawn done set remains live until a later same-body await_all drains the exact set before nested repeat re-entry. await_any remains observation-only, including prior observations before the do, post-do observations, and second post-spawn observations; it never replaces the mandatory final await_all when more than one generated child is pending.

Within that rule, an accepted blocking do may run while generated spawns are already pending, may run after a prior multi-pending await_any observation, and may be followed by one or more later generated spawns before the final drain. The documented top-level when and switch branch paths mirror each other. Missing same-body drains, cross-domain activation without an explicit crossing, deeper branch/loop nesting, implicit CDC, dynamic generated-child specialization, and broader outstanding-child lifetime semantics remain fail-closed.

Generated-child actor-to-actor and pin route support is intentionally small. Each route uses one direct source, one direct sink, deterministic generated handoffs, and one named drive-call cycle. Actor-to-actor route width is either scalar one-bit or the exact matching child endpoint width. Multiple actor-to-actor routes are accepted only when they share the same source child, sink child, parent transaction, contiguous route segment, and matching endpoint widths per route. Pin-ingress route width is scalar one-bit for the scalar multi-route subset, one exact matching top-input/child-input vector width for the one-route vector subset, or route-local exact matching top-input/child-input widths for the same-child vector multi-route subset. The same-child mixed pin-ingress subset accepts scalar one-bit routes and exact-width vector routes together while preserving route-local kind, width, and width_source. Pin-egress route width is scalar one-bit for the scalar multi-route subset, one exact matching child-output/top-output vector width for the one-route vector subset, or route-local exact matching child-output/top-output widths for the same-child vector multi-route subset. The same-child mixed pin-egress subset accepts scalar one-bit routes and exact-width vector routes together while preserving route-local kind, width, and width_source. Multiple scalar pin-ingress routes are accepted only when they share one resolved child, one parent transaction, unique top-level input pins, unique child input endpoints, and adjacent pre-trigger drive calls; multiple pin-egress routes are accepted only when they share one resolved child, one parent transaction, unique child output endpoints, unique top-level output pins, and adjacent post-event drive calls. Generated-handoff remapping or reuse, fan-in/fan-out data routing, route mux/storage, CDC/reset remapping, ready/backpressure, payload protocols, parameterized route drive definitions, route drive-call actual arguments, recursive actor networks, and permanent actor grouping remain outside the shipped subset.

Malformed or width-mismatched generated-child actor-to-actor route shapes still fail closed with targeted diagnostics before FSMGen infers remapping, storage, muxing, payload adaptation, fan-in/fan-out, or backpressure behavior.
